etymarab.kok_maddesi: Back to library EtymArab ĠZː (ĠZZ) غزّ / غزز BP – • HDAL • © SG | 15Oct2024 √ĠZː(ĠZZ) "root" ▪ ĠZː (ĠZZ)_1 ‘to be thorny, prickly; to prick’ ↗ ʔaġazza ▪ ĠZː (ĠZZ)_2 ‘Gaza (port in Palestine)’ ↗ Ġazzaẗᵘ ▪ ĠZː (ĠZZ)_3 ‘gauze’ ↗ ġazzī Other values, now obsolete, include (Hava1899): ▪ † ĠZː (ĠZZ)_4 ‘to become attached, cleave ( bi to s.o.)’: † ġazza ( u , ġazaz ) and † ĭġtazza (VIII); cf. also L-stem † ġāzza (III) ‘to wrestle, contend with s.o.’ and Lt-stem † taġāzza (VI) ‘to quarrel (about s.th)’ ▪ † ĠZː (ĠZZ)_5 ‘philanthropists’: † ġuzzāz ▪ † ĠZː (ĠZZ)_ ‘…’ ↗ … ▪ [v1] : In MSA, the *Š-stem ʔaġazza (form IV) is the only form of the vb. that expresses the notion of ‘being thorny, prickly, pricking’. Historically, also the G-stem † ġazza ( u , ġazz ) is attested with the meaning ‘to prick (a needle, fī into)’; cf. also the corresponding N-stem † ĭnġazza (VII) ‘to penetrate, sink ( fī into)’. ▪ [v2] : (Gesenius1915:) Given the Akk forms in ḫ‑ and the fact that in Grk, Gáza is older than the Byzantine form Aza , one may assume that initial ġ‑ (as in Ar) was prior to ʕ‑ (as in Hbr or Min) and that Ar thus has preserved the more original phonetics; yet, the name of the port city in Southern Palestine that was one of the 5 major cities of the Philisters, seems to be related to Sem *ʕZZ (see Ar ↗ʕZː (ʕZZ)) ‘strength, to be strong’ rather than to ĠZː (ĠZZ)_1 ‘to be horny, pricky’. ▪ [v3] : ġazzī may be a nsb-formation from [v2] Ġazzaẗ , in which case ‘gauze’ would be the tissue *‘from Gaza’. Other theories trace the Eur words back to Ar ↗ qazz ‘raw silk’, or both the Ar and the Eur words to a Pers keǧ ‘id.’ – EtymOnline, Osman2002, Vennemann2006 (following Tazi1998). ▪ † [v4] : Are the vb.s listed above from [v1] so that ‘becoming attached, cleaving to s.o.’ (I, VIII) and ‘wrestling, quarreling’ (III, VI) would essentially be a *‘pricking’? ▪ † [v5] : The term † ġuzzāz ‘philanthropists’ is completely obscure. ▪ … – ▪ [v1] : apparently without cognates in Sem or elsewhere. ▪ [v2] : (Gesenius1915:) Akk Ḫazzatu , Ḫazzutu , Ḫaziti , Amarna Azzati , Ḫazati , Hbr ʕazzāʰ , Min ʕzt , Ar Ġazzaẗ ; outside Sem: Eg Gaṣat(u) . ▪ [v3] : see prob.
